- [Cover 3](../06-pass-coverage/06-03-cover-3-family.qmd), [Cover 2 and Tampa 2](../06-pass-coverage/06-04-cover-2-and-tampa-2.qmd)
  and [Quarters and Match](../06-pass-coverage/06-05-quarters-and-match.qmd): each coverage chapter says who the force
  and the alley player are, because the coverage decides it.
- [Disguise and Rotation](../06-pass-coverage/06-06-disguise-rotation-and-split-field.qmd): how a defense hides which
  safety will be the plus-one until the snap.
- [Zone Blitz and Simulated Pressure](../07-pressure/07-03-zone-blitz-and-simulated-pressure.qmd): gap exchanges
  aimed at the pass protection instead of the run.
- [Constraint Theory and Sequencing](../08-the-chess-match/08-02-constraint-theory-and-sequencing.qmd): play-action and
  RPOs as the offense's answer to defenders whose run fits pull them out of coverage.
- [The Modern Era](../11-history/11-05-the-modern-era.qmd): the two-high counterrevolution and the light-box run game.

**See also (case studies):** [The Ravens' Option Run Game](../12-case-studies/12-05-ravens-lamar-run-game.qmd), box math
with a quarterback who counts as a blocker; and [Fangio's Two-High Revolution and Macdonald's
Answer](../12-case-studies/12-08-two-high-to-macdonald.qmd), the light box as a whole defensive philosophy.

**If you want to go deeper:** Cody Alexander's MatchQuarters site and books, the most thorough public writing on how
two-high defenses fit the run; Jon Svec's short essays on defending specific run schemes, spill and box included; Chris
B. Brown's *The Art of Smart Football* on how run schemes and defenses answer each other; and any broadcast's end-zone
replay of a power run, watched only for the end man and the man outside him.

[^svec]: Jon Svec, "Defending Split Zone" (January 12, 2022): spill players "fight INSIDE the blocker by using a Wrong
    Arm Technique," which requires another defender to take the gap outside; a boxing end should "stonewall the Slice Block
    [split zone's kick-out] and set the edge," keeping his "outside arm free":
    <https://jonsvec.substack.com/p/defending-split-zone>. Coaching vocabulary varies: some staffs say *squeeze* or
    *lever* for box technique, and *wrong-arm* or *wrong-shoulder* for spill.

[^fitwords]: Ed Raby Jr., "Simplifying Your 2nd Level Run Fits," American Football Coaches Association (May 9, 2023):
    a "force/fold" player is "the widest underneath defender outside the run box," keeping "near-shoulder leverage on the
    ball carrier," and the "spill" player fits "inside out on the near hip of the ball carrier"; in Cover 3 the strong
    safety is a force player, and in Cover 2 the corners are force:
    <https://www.afca.com/simplifying-your-2nd-level-run-fits/>. For the two-high version, see Cody Alexander's
    MatchQuarters (<https://www.matchquarters.com>).

[^heavy]: James Reber, Next Gen Stats, "NFL trend watch: heavy personnel" (February 2026): offenses used fewer than three
    wide receivers on 41.7% of plays in 2025:
    <https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-trend-watch-heavy-personnel-could-shape-super-bowl-lx-showdown-between-patriots-and-seahawks>
    (planning/FACTS-current.md §10).

[^quarters]: NFL Next Gen Stats: Cover 4 was used on 17.2% of plays in 2025, against a 2018–2024 average of
    13.9%; Cover 3 remains more common (planning/FACTS-current.md §10). Same article as the split-safety rates cited
    below.

[^twohigh]: NFL Next Gen Stats, split-safety coverage rate: 32.9% (2018), 40.4% (2024), 42.0% (2025):
    <https://www.nfl.com/news/the-coverage-that-turned-the-seahawks-into-super-bowl-winners-and-is-taking-the-nfl-by-storm>.

[^lightshare]: This book's calculation from nflverse play-by-play joined to participation data (`defenders_in_box`),
    regular-season designed runs (quarterback scrambles and kneels excluded): six or fewer in the box on 37–40% of
    designed runs each season from 2018 to 2022, 43% in 2023, 58% in 2024 and 55% in 2025. The box count comes from Next
    Gen Stats through 2022 and from FTN charting from 2023, so part of the change may be how the box is counted; the jump
    from 2023 to 2024 is within the FTN years.

[^fangio]: Fangio (born 1958): San Francisco defensive coordinator 2011–2014, Chicago defensive coordinator 2015–2018,
    Denver head coach 2019–2021, Eagles consultant 2022, Miami defensive coordinator 2023, Philadelphia defensive
    coordinator from 2024 (still in 2026, planning/FACTS-current.md §9). His first NFL job was Saints linebackers coach
    in 1986, so he spent 32 NFL seasons as an assistant before Denver hired him in January 2019:
    <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vic_Fangio>. Staley worked under Fangio in Chicago and Denver before running the
    Rams' defense (2020) and coaching the Chargers (2021–2023); Diante Lee, "Checking in on the Vic Fangio coaching tree
    after Week 1 of the 2021 NFL season," PFF (September 15, 2021), on Staley, Joe Barry and Sean Desai carrying the
    scheme: <https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-vic-fangio-coaching-tree-week-1-2021>.

[^inq]: EJ Smith, "Eagles run defense ... Vic Fangio," *Philadelphia Inquirer* (September 19, 2024): a light box forces
    the linemen to "win at the point of attack and, at times, 'steal' back gaps":
    <https://www.inquirer.com/eagles/eagles-run-defense-vic-fangio-jalen-carter-falcons-bijan-robinson-20240919.html>.

[^heavy2]: Next Gen Stats (Reber), same article as above: defenses played base on 29.7% of plays in 2025, against a low
    of 20.5% in 2023 (planning/FACTS-current.md §10).

[^fangiocalc]: This book's calculation from nflverse play-by-play and participation data, 2024 regular season,
    opponents' designed runs: the Eagles faced six or fewer in the box on 66% of them (third-highest rate; league 58%)
    and allowed −0.18 EPA per designed run, the lowest of the 32 defenses.

[^boxepa]: This book's calculation, same filters as the chart, both eras pooled: designed runs averaged −0.03,
    −0.05, −0.09 and −0.15 EPA against 5-or-fewer, 6, 7 and 8-or-more defenders in the box (success rates 41%, 40%, 37%
    and 34%; 5.1, 4.8, 4.6 and 4.2 yards per carry; about 1,600, 21,800, 20,100 and 6,700 runs). Dropbacks averaged
    +0.06, +0.08, +0.12 and +0.16 EPA.

[^seattle]: "Seattle Cover 3 defense," Wikipedia (the scheme of Pete Carroll and Dan Quinn; Seattle led the NFL in
    scoring defense from 2012 to 2015; Thomas as the post safety, Chancellor in the box):
    <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Cover_3_defense>; "Legion of Boom," Wikipedia:
    <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_of_Boom>.

[^inq2]: EJ Smith, *Philadelphia Inquirer*, September 19, 2024 (cited above): six or fewer in the box on "73.5% of the
    time, which is the NFL's third-highest rate," written after the Eagles' Week 2 loss to Atlanta.

[^fangiocalc2]: This book's calculation from nflverse play-by-play and participation data, regular seasons, opponents'
    designed runs: the share of runs Fangio's defenses faced with six or fewer in the box ranked 5th (Denver 2019), 2nd
    (2020), 3rd (2021), 2nd (Miami 2023), 3rd (Philadelphia 2024) and 3rd (2025) of 32 defenses; by average box count,
    7th, 2nd, 3rd, 10th, 5th and 5th lightest. EPA per designed run allowed ranked 1st in 2024 and 7th in 2025. Super Bowl
    LIX, Eagles 40, Chiefs 22: planning/FACTS-current.md §1.

[^ravens]: "Ravens break single-season team rushing record," NFL.com (3,296 yards, breaking the 1978 Patriots' 3,165):
    <https://www.nfl.com/news/ravens-break-single-season-team-rushing-record-0ap3000001092761>; Jackson's 1,206 rushing
    yards and unanimous MVP: <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Baltimore_Ravens_season>. The era is closed: John
    Harbaugh was fired in January 2026 (planning/FACTS-current.md §0, C3).

[^ravenscalc]: This book's calculation from nflverse play-by-play and participation data (Next Gen Stats box counts),
    2019 regular season, designed runs: Baltimore faced seven or more in the box on 65% (league 62%); EPA per designed
    run +0.10 against seven (league −0.10) and +0.04 against eight or more (league −0.13); Baltimore led the league at
    +0.09 EPA per designed run overall. Jackson: 120 designed runs, 7.1 yards per carry.

[^barkley]: NFL.com, "Saquon Barkley becomes ninth player to rush for 2,000 yards in a season":
    <https://www.nfl.com/news/saquon-barkley-becomes-ninth-player-to-rush-for-2000-yards-in-a-season>.

[^eaglescalc]: This book's calculation from nflverse play-by-play, participation and FTN charting, 2024 regular season,
    designed runs excluding quarterback sneaks (FTN `is_qb_sneak`): Philadelphia ran into six or fewer in the box on 61%
